ranking.note: Promoted: LevelDB's exclusive lock is the hard blocker that stops any external consumer from reading block/header data while a node runs, i.e. a category-defining limitation, not just a feature gap.
Moved up: it is the most concrete step of the kernel's core decoupling work (removing util/translation.h, tracking issue #27587) and sits in the same error-handling chain as #29700.
Raised from P3: it is the competing design decision to #33847/#30342 on the shape of the kernel logging API before stabilization, so it carries the same consequence as those P2s.

inconsistencies: Direct design conflict: #34775 restricts libbitcoinkernel to a single process-global logging connection, while #33847 + #30342 add per-context connections with per-connection levels and per-context routing. They cannot both be right; a decision is needed before either lands. Review #33847 (the fuller design, plus #30342) first and treat #34775 as the fallback if per-context logging is rejected.

Logging chain order matters: #33847 (API shape, depends on #34374) must precede #30342 (per-context delivery, also depends on #34778, #29256, #33847); #30342 in turn unblocks wallet-side work in #30343.

Three overlapping fatal/runtime error refactors at the kernel boundary: #29700 (return util::Result/FlushResult instead of AbortNode), #36326 (typed FatalError/FlushError replacing bilingual_str in notifications) and #35646 (RFC removing M_ERROR from ValidationState via util::Expected). They rework the same surface and risk duplicating each other; review #29700 first as the base (it is built on #25665), then #36326, then decide whether #35646's RFC is still needed.

#36318 (BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE / always-set invalid result) and #35646 both redefine ValidationState semantics and the kernel C API's validation error reporting; whichever lands first will force rework on the other.

Kernel + validation overlap, likely needing a split as the category file warns: #32427 rewrites block-tree storage, #35187 adds a check-only ConnectBlock path with a custom coins view, #36318 also changes net processing, and #35662 is mostly a validation-side change to PrecomputedTransactionData with only an incidental kernel C API copy fix.
result.notes: The category is dominated by P2 API-capability and decoupling work, which is expected here; only #32427 was raised to P1 because its problem (no concurrent external reader access) is the one that currently makes the library unusable for the stated downstream use cases. Pure API trimming and documentation (#33820, #36353) stay P3 per the category rule on cosmetic polish, and #35662 stays P4 as an unmeasured micro-optimization.
